patients.label: 16-year-old woman with chronic immune thrombocytopenia and alopecia areata, treated with baricitinib
attribution_limitations: The text prints a platelet count of 6 × 10^(9 )/L from the blood tests (Table 1) while the Table 1 platelet row prints 7 × 10^(9)/L. Both are kept as review-only source-conflict facts.
Table 1 prints hemoglobin as 660 g/L against a printed range of 110–156 g/L, while the text reports a marked microcytic anemia; the printed value is implausible but kept as printed and not corrected.

Table 1 is titled Complementary tests at diagnosis and prints anti-microsomal antibodies of 8547 U/ml, while the text says the anti-microsomal (anti-TPO) antibodies (8,547 UI/ml) were measured later, when corticosteroids were discontinued. The unit is spelled U/ml, UI/ml and IU/ml in different places. The discussion also places the high anti-TPO titers just before baricitinib treatment.

Table 1 lists the autoimmune screening rows and the NGS panel under tests at diagnosis, while the text describes the screening (citing Table 1) and the NGS panel after the anti-microsomal measurement when corticosteroids were discontinued. The table-only rows keep the caption time; the screening text fact and the NGS fact (table row and text describe the same single 192-gene panel with the same result) carry no time, and their event is ordered only before baricitinib by the word then.
The authors state that the link between baricitinib and the platelet improvement remains speculative and that spontaneous ITP remission may have occurred; no causal fact is recorded.
The 12-day follow-up platelet count is printed as 6 × 10^(9) without /L; no unit is added.
The discussion says the anti-TPO findings could be coincidental and that thyroid disease as a cause of a secondary ITP cannot be confirmed; no thyroid or secondary-ITP condition is recorded.
Figure 1 prints an IVIG dose of 1g/kg body weight and an AA complete response marker that the text does not state; these are pixel content in visual.json only.

events.description: Physical examination with paleness, petechiae and a scalp alopecia patch

events.description: Blood tests and peripheral blood smear (Table 1)

evidence.quote: Blood tests (Table 1) showed a marked microcytic anemia, high reticulocyte count and severe thrombocytopenia of 6 × 10^(9 )/L.

A ferritin level of 8.60 ng/ml was noted, consistent with iron deficiency anemia, as well as a moderate increase in liver enzymes.
There were no other significant findings.
